2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that, opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted a suit for realisation of loan in the Court of the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Chittagong being Money Execution Case No. 36 of 1990, against the petitioner and others and ultimately obtained decree therein on contest. Thereafter, the plaintiff decree holder started Execution Case No.2 of 1994 for satisfaction of the aforesaid decree. While the execution case was in progress before the learned Artha Rin Adalat, the petitioner filed an application before the Court under Order 21 rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceedings of Money Execution Case in question on the ground that one of the judgment-debtors has already filed Other Class Suit No. 20 of 1992 before the 1st Court of Chittagong challenging the decree under execution. 

 3. The decree-holder opposite party resisted the aforesaid application denying its material allegations and contended, inter alia, that Order 21 rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no mariner of application in the case and, as such, the application is liable to be rejected. The learned Artha Rin Adalat by his impugned order dated 9-3-97 rejected the petitioner''s application under Order 21 rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 4. Mr Matiar Rahman, learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, submits that since Other Class Suit No. 20 of 1992 has already been started by one of the judgment-debtors against the decree-holder in respect of the money in question, the learned Artha Rin Adalat and Subordinate Judge erred in law in rejecting the petitioner''s application under Order 21 rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 "Where a suit is pending in any Court against the holder of a decree of such Court, on the part of the person against whom the decree was passed, the Court may, on such terms as to security or otherwise, as it thinks fit, stay execution of the decree until the pending suit has been decided." 

 It is evident from rule 29 that where a suit is pending in any Court against the holder of decree of such Court, on the part of the person against whom the decree was passed, the Court may on such terms as to security or otherwise stay the execution of the decree till the pending suit has been decided. The first requirement of law of application of Order 21 rule 29 of the Code is that the subsequent suit must be pending before the same Court which passed the decree in the earlier suit and that it must be filed by the judgment debtor. In this case, there is no dispute to the fact that the learned Subordinate-Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Chittagong passed the impugned decree and Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1992 is pending before the same Court but Money Suit No. 20 of 1992 filed by one of the judgment-debtors is pending not before the Artha Rin Adalat Rin Adalat No. 3 but before the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong. It is thus manifestly clear that the two Courts are not the same Courts but are different Courts with defined jurisdiction. So, it is evident that Order 21 rule 29 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
